title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Natural History of Atrial Arrhythmias in Patients With Systemic Right Ventricle.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The incidence and risk factors for atrial arrhythmia (AA; atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter) in adults with systemic right ventricle (sRV), specifically congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries and dextro-transposition of the great arteries palliated with atrial switch procedures, are not well understood. This study aims to better define these risks.

METHODS: Adults with sRV presenting to Mayo Clinic between 2000 and 2022 were identified. Their clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic parameters at the time of first presentation were recorded. The incidence of sustained AA (>30 seconds) during follow-up was documented. Cox regression analysis was used to identify associations of incident atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter and mortality during follow-up.

RESULTS: Among 447 patients with sRV (median age, 33.1 [24.6-42.8], 55.9% male, 247 cm3-TGA; 200 dextro-transposition of the great arteries postatrial switch), AA was present at first visit in 113 (25.3%). Out of the remaining 334 patients, new-onset AA occurred in 125 (37.4%) patients during a median follow-up of 11.1 years (interquartile range, 3.6-19.3). Isolated atrial fibrillation was observed in 89 (37.4%), isolated atrial flutter in 76 (31.9%), and both atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter in 73 (30.7%) patients. In multivariable analysis, the risk factors for incident AA included age (hazard ratio, 1.04 [1.03-1.06]; P<0.001), d-TGA (hazard ratio, 1.96 [1.00-3.85]; P=0.05), and QRS duration (hazard ratio, 1.01 [1.00-1.02]; P=0.02). AA was associated with hospitalization for heart failure in 19% of patients. Among those treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs and ablation, recurrence occurred in over 50% of patients. AA was not an independent predictor of mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: AA occurred in more than half of this cohort with sRV, with risk increasing significantly after the third decade of life. Advancing age, dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and prolonged QRS duration were associated with increased risk of AA. Close monitoring for AA and early interventions are warranted in all adults with sRV.

title: Late pacemaker lead perforation in acute myopericarditis: a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Although myocarditis can be associated with ventricular wall thinning, aneurysm, and free wall rupture, late pacemaker lead perforation in myopericarditis is previously unreported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 71-year-old man with a dual-chamber pacemaker placed 7 years prior presented with acute myopericarditis 2 months after atrial fibrillation ablation, left ventricular ejection fraction of 52%, and small pericardial effusion. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) revealed focal late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of the basal inferolateral wall of the left ventricle. Diffuse, circumferential pericardial LGE was present around the left and right ventricle with small effusion. One month later, he returned with worsening chest pain, decompensated heart failure, moderate pericardial effusion, and effusive-constrictive physiology. Echocardiography identified a new pacemaker lead perforation. Following device revision, he was discharged on colchicine, non steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and empagliflozin. On follow-up, ejection fraction normalized, and constrictive physiology and cardiac inflammation resolved.

DISCUSSION: Late lead perforation is a rare complication of myopericarditis and should be considered in patients who re-present with progressive pericardial effusion and decompensation after initial improvement.

title: Device embolization after percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation who are unsuitable for long-term anticoagulation. Although device embolization is rare, it represents a potentially catastrophic complication. Robust contemporary data on its incidence, timing, determinants, and clinical consequences are limited. To provide contemporary, comprehensive estimates of device embolization after percutaneous LAAO and to identify factors associated with embolization risk and related mortality.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting device embolization after LAAO, as well as embolization-related mortality. Random-effects models were applied to estimate pooled embolization incidence and case-fatality rates. Subgroup analyses were performed by device type and device family. Exploratory meta-regression assessed sources of heterogeneity, including publication year and study sample size.

RESULTS: Seventy-three studies, including seventy observational studies and three randomized controlled trials, involving 97 316 patients, were analysed. The pooled embolization incidence was .31% [95% confidence interval (CI) .19%-.50%]. Among studies reporting embolization timing, 80% of events occurred within 24 h of implantation. Larger sample size and more recent publication year were independently associated with lower embolization risk. Device-specific incidence was lowest for Watchman FLX (.02%) and Watchman 2.5 (.12%), and higher for Amplatzer Cardiac Plug (1.02%) and Amulet (.43%). Embolization-related mortality was 10.61% (95% CI 4.98%-21.16%), with no evidence of temporal improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Device embolization after LAAO is infrequent and has declined substantially over time, likely reflecting technological advances and procedural experience. However, when embolization occurs, it remains associated with high mortality, underscoring the importance of careful device selection and optimized implantation strategies.

Preferential Conduction Along the Epicardial Ventricular Septum During Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Basal LV Summit: A Pitfall for Anatomical Ablation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: An anatomical ablation of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) originating from the left ventricular summit (LVS) is delivered from endocardial sites across the myocardium adjacent to the site of the VA origin with the guidance of transvenous epicardial mapping. Therefore, electrophysiological information obtained by transvenous epicardial mapping should be carefully interpreted.

OBJECTIVES: This study investigated ventricular activation patterns within the great cardiac vein (GCV) during idiopathic LVS VAs.

METHODS: We studied 38 consecutive patients who underwent a successful endocardial ablation of idiopathic LVS VAs at the left ostial process, left coronary sinus, and commissure between the left and right coronary cusps.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients exhibited a radial activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded around the junction between the GCV and anterior interventricular vein (AIVV). The remaining 9 patients exhibited a septal activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded within the AIVV, with the activation sequence being from the AIVV to GCV. The septal group mainly exhibited left bundle branch block pattern, whereas the radial group exhibited right bundle branch block pattern (P < 0.0001). The distance between the earliest ventricular activation site within the GCV or AIVV and the successful ablation site was significantly larger for LVS VAs with a septal activation pattern than those with a radial activation pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: During idiopathic basal LVS VAs, activation from those VA origins often preferentially conducted along the ventricular septum. It should be kept in mind that this unusual activation pattern may mislead the mapping and catheter ablation of LVS VAs.

title: Discontinuation of Anticoagulation in Patients at Relatively High Risk of Stroke After Successful Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulant (OAC) discontinuation after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation may be feasible in selected patients; however, outcomes in those at high stroke risk remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate associations between OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after ablation and thromboembolic or bleeding events across CHA2DS2-VA risk strata.

METHODS: Patients without AF recurrence within 12 months of catheter ablation and with CHA2DS2-VA scores ≥2 were identified from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database and classified as OAC continuers or discontinuers based on prescription coverage at the 12-month landmark. The primary outcome was a composite of stroke or systemic embolism and major bleeding. Doubly robust estimation combined overlap weighting with covariate-adjusted Cox regression, stratified by CHA2DS2-VA score (2-4 and ≥5).

RESULTS: Among 3,637 patients (mean age: 60.8 ± 9.7 years, 27.1% female, mean CHA2DS2-VA 3.2 ± 1.3), discontinuation in those with scores of 2-4 (n = 3,054) was associated with lower risks of the composite event (HR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.38-0.96) and major bleeding (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.29-0.90), without increased stroke or systemic embolism (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.34-1.58). In those with scores ≥5 (n = 583), discontinuation was not significantly associated with any outcome, and tests for interaction were not significant (all P > 0.46).

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA2DS2-VA score 2 to 4.

title: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy in Pakistan: A Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes, Maternal and Obstetric Characteristics
summary: Abstract Background Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is an important cause of maternal cardiovascular mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries due to limited access to specialized cardiac care. This systematic review aims to synthesize evidence on the proportions of mortality, recovery of left ventricular function, cardiovascular complications, and maternal and obstetric characteristics among women with PPCM in Pakistan. Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Google Scholar, PakMediNet, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2026 for studies reporting PPCM outcomes in Pakistan and registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420261403054). Eligible studies included observational studies and case series involving women diagnosed with PPCM. Extracted data included study design, sample size, mortality, recovery of left ventricular systolic function, cardiovascular complications, and obstetric characteristics. Pooled proportions were calculated descriptively using aggregate study data. The quality of study was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Results Seven studies were included. Mortality outcomes were reported in six studies including 315 patients, with 49 deaths recorded, yielding an overall mortality proportion of 15.6%. Recovery of left ventricular systolic function was reported in four studies including 160 patients, of whom 97 achieved recoveries, corresponding to an overall recovery proportion of 60.6%, predominantly defined by improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction during 6–12 months of follow-up. Pulmonary edema was the most frequently reported cardiovascular complication (21.6%), while thromboembolic events (17.9%), cardiogenic shock (13.1%), ventricular tachycardia (9.9%), and atrial fibrillation (9.4%) occurred less frequently. Among the reported maternal characteristics, obesity was the most common (62.9%). Multiparity was the predominant obstetric characteristic (69.1%), whereas pregnancy-related hypertensive disorders, primigravidity, and multiple gestation were reported in 34.1%, 22.9%, and 9.7% of women, respectively. Conclusion PPCM in Pakistan remains associated with considerable mortality and a substantial burden of cardiovascular complications. Obesity, multiparity, and pregnancy-related hypertensive disorders were the predominant maternal and obstetric characteristics, highlighting the importance of early recognition, timely cardiac assessment, and multidisciplinary care to improve maternal outcomes. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

title: Short-term and intermittent ECG-based screening for atrial fibrillation in older adults without known atrial fibrillation: a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of randomized trials with time-to-event data.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive ECG-based screening for atrial fibrillation (AF) in older adults may increase detection of silent AF and uptake of oral anticoagulation (OAC), but screening strategies, AF definitions, AF burden, and downstream treatment thresholds vary across trials.

METHODS: We performed a a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing short-term or intermittent non-invasive ECG-based AF screening strategies versus usual care, opportunistic detection, or no invitation in older adults without known AF. For dichotomous outcomes, pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) assessed conclusiveness of evidence.

RESULTS: Across seven RCTs involving 77,526 participants (38,770 assigned to ECG-based screening and 38,756 to control group), screening increased new AF diagnoses compared with control (RR 1.76, 95% CI 1.21-2.56; moderate-certainty). ECG-based screening also increased new OAC initiation (RR 1.78, 95% CI 1.13-2.81; moderate-certainty). However, there were no significant differences in stroke or systemic embolism (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.89-1.01), all-cause mortality (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.95-1.02), or major bleeding (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.92-1.05). Exploratory subgroup analyses by screening framework did not show statistically significant subgroup differences for AF detection, stroke/systemic embolism, mortality, or major bleeding. TSA indicated that evidence for AF detection and clinical outcomes remains inconclusive.

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term and intermittent ECG-based AF screening in older adults without known AF increases trial-defined AF detection and OAC initiation but has not demonstrated reductions in stroke, mortality, or major bleeding. Current evidence supports a cautious, risk-based screening approach rather than broad population-wide implementation.

title: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation in children and young adults with severe adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre experience.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Left cardiac sympathetic denervation is established for selected high-risk inherited arrhythmia syndromes, but evidence for an intended bilateral strategy in children and young adults remains limited. We evaluated the rationale, feasibility, safety, follow-up ascertainment, and outcomes of intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation.

METHODS: Consecutive children and young adults undergoing intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation between January 2015 and November 2025 were reviewed. The operation targeted the lower stellate component and upper thoracic sympathetic chain bilaterally, usually through single-port thoracoscopic access. Outcomes were obtained from specialist cardiology follow-up, electrocardiography, Holter monitoring, exercise testing when available, inpatient telemetry, device interrogation, and medication records.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients were operated. Mean age was 12.4 years. Bilateral denervation was completed in 36 patients; 1 underwent left-sided denervation only owing to intraoperative haemodynamic instability. Single-port access was used in 30 patients. There were no intraoperative deaths, unplanned full thoracotomy conversions, intercostal injuries, reoperations for surgical complications, or denervation-related permanent pacing. Procedure-attributable morbidity comprised one mild Horner syndrome and one self-limited axillary wound complaint. Among 36 patients with post-discharge follow-up, 32 remained free from the primary malignant ventricular arrhythmic endpoint. Estimated malignant ventricular arrhythmia-free survival was 95.8 per cent at 1 year and 89.4 per cent at 3 years.

CONCLUSION: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation was feasible and had low procedure-attributable morbidity in selected young patients. It should be interpreted as an adjunct to multidisciplinary arrhythmia care, not as a replacement for medication, device surveillance, or follow-up.

title: The influence of genotype on clinical outcomes in dilated cardiomyopathy.
summary:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmia (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (ESHF) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) may vary by genotype. Comparative analyses remain limited. The aim of this study was to compare clinical outcomes and risk predictors across genotypes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Carriers of pathogenic variants in DCM-associated genes were identified from a dedicated database. Clinically affected variant-carriers from the five most prevalent genotypes were compared with genotype-negative patients. A composite primary endpoint consisted of MVA or ESHF. Secondary endpoints were MVA and ESHF individually. Incidence rates and baseline variables associated with outcomes were evaluated.Among 484 patients, 57 (11.8%) met the primary endpoint after 5 years. Genotype-negative patients had the lowest primary endpoint incidence rates [1.4 (0.7-2.1) per 100 person-years], whereas LMNA had the highest [6.2 (3.0-9.5)]. With a genotype-negative reference, incidence rate ratios were 1.3 for TTN, 1.7 for FLNC, 2.0 for DSP, 2.7 for RBM20 and 4.4 for LMNA. Rates were higher in LMNA and RBM20 than genotype-negative patients (P < .001 and P = .003, respectively) and higher in LMNA than TTN (P = .001). Results were similar for MVA. LMNA had higher ESHF rates than genotype-negative, TTN and DSP.Left ventricular diastolic diameter, LMNA variants and late gadolinium enhancement were independently associated with the primary endpoint. Baseline predictors varied by genotype.

CONCLUSION: Genotype stratification in DCM reveals a risk hierarchy with risk lowest in genotype-negative and TTN patients, two-fold higher in DSP and FLNC, and three- and four-fold higher in RBM20 and LMNA, respectively. Accounting for genotype improves risk prediction.

Quantitative membranous septum area assessment with advanced three-dimensional CT visualization with a mixed reality-capable device.
summary:
AIMS: Permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rates remained elevated for patients receiving transcatheter aortic valve implantation for aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation. Therefore, detailed assessment of the membranous septum (MS) anatomy is essential to understand the mechanism and mitigate risk. This study aims to examine the accuracy and reproducibility of a novel 3D hologram system to measure transcatheter aortic valve implantation-related aortic valvar complex anatomy and present a novel methodology to measure MS area with it.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Cardiac computer tomography series of AS, aortic regurgitation, and coronary artery disease (CAD) patient cohorts were analysed using CarnaLife Holo (MedApp SA, Kraków, Poland) to quantify and compare their MS areas. 3mensio Structural Heart was used as a benchmark comparator, with annulus area (AA) selected as the quantitative parameter. Intraclass correlation coefficient values between the software all exceeded 0.99, with no statistically significant difference noted between AA measurements. Bland-Altman plotting illustrated narrow boundaries of agreement, with no significant outliers. In interobserver agreement analysis for 3D hologram, AA measurements were not significantly different between two investigators (P = 0.906). No significant difference was found between the MS areas between the three cohorts after ANOVA testing (P = 0.1640).

CONCLUSION: 3D holographic software provides a feasible and reproducible tool for visualising and measuring the aortic valvar complex anatomy. In addition, its ability to assess the shape, pattern, and area of the MS offers anatomic insights not readily available with other software.

title: Case Report: Rupture of multiple perforating branches and fatal giant interventricular septal hematoma: a severe complication of left bundle branch area pacing.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is generally safe. Giant interventricular septal hematoma (IVSH) is an extremely rare complication of LBBAP. Previously reported cases had favorable outcomes, and no fatal cases have been reported to date.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old male with 4 years of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and refractory heart failure (HF) had a preoperative left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 13.2% and left bundle branch block. Following HF stabilization, cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator (CRTD) implantation was performed. Intraoperative LBBAP correction was unsatisfactory, and left ventricular lead placement failed. The patient developed chest pain and hypotension 5 h postoperatively. Bedside echocardiography detected a giant IVSH causing biventricular compression and pericardial effusion. Despite emergency extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support, pericardial drainage and interventional embolization, his condition worsened rapidly. Coronary angiography (CAG) identified rupture of multiple septal perforator branches. He succumbed to irreversible circulatory collapse 10 h after surgery.

CONCLUSION: Although most patients with LBBAP-associated IVSH achieve a favorable prognosis with timely intervention, the condition can progress rapidly and pose a life-threatening risk in those with end-stage severe HF.

Variability and Drivers of Battery Longevity in Contemporary Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Systems Across Geographic Regions.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Battery longevity of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) and cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillators (CRT-Ds) affects clinical outcomes and resource use, yet the contribution of regional practice patterns to battery consumption remains poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVES: We compared projected battery longevity of contemporary ICD and CRT-D systems across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and North America and evaluated factors associated with regional differences.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 138,897 transvenous ICD/CRT-D devices (market release 2019) from 36 countries in the global BIOTRONIK Home Monitoring database. Longevity was estimated using a validated linear battery-drain projection model. Devices were grouped by type and geographic region.

RESULTS: Median (Q1-Q3) longevity was highest for single-chamber ICD (14.8 [Q1-Q3: 14.0-15.5] years) and lowest for CRT-D (9.3 [Q1-Q3: 7.9-10.5] years). Longevity was longer in Asia-Pacific and Europe than in North America, with the longest estimates observed in Asia-Pacific subregional clusters and regional differences up to 2.0 years. High-voltage consumption showed limited regional variation. Larger differences were observed for low-voltage consumption and atrial pacing burden (8.7%-40.1%). Remote monitoring contributed <1% to battery drain, whereas telemetry-related energy consumption for in-office visits exhibited the greatest regional variability. Multivariable analyses identified pacing burden, follow-up intensity, and delivered shocks as independent correlates of projected battery longevity. Adjustment for these factors attenuated, but did not eliminate, regional differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Battery longevity of contemporary ICD/CRT-D systems varies substantially across geographic regions despite identical device technology, and may be potentially extended by attention to pacing-related device use and follow-up methods.

title: Pooled Periprocedural and Short-Term Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Contemporary Self-Expanding Valves: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary self-expanding transcatheter heart valves (SEVs) have incorporated design refinements to reduce paravalvular leak (PVL) and pacemaker implantation (PPI). We aimed to characterize clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with contemporary SEVs in patients with severe aortic stenosis.

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus were searched through October 5, 2025, for studies reporting procedural, hemodynamic, and clinical outcomes for patients undergoing TAVR with the (1) Navitor or (2) Evolut PRO/PRO+/FX. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled single-arm event rates, stratified by SEV group, using the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. Between-platform differences were assessed using subgroup interaction testing.

RESULTS: Fifty-two studies (n = 21,349; weighted mean age 82 years; mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality 4.8%) were included. At 30 days, all-cause mortality was low among Evolut and Navitor cohorts (1.4 and 1.5%; p = 0.63), and device success was high for both platforms (92.1 and 93.0%; p = 0.73). Moderate or greater PVL occurred in 2.5 and 1.1% of Evolut and Navitor cohorts, respectively (p = 0.12), mild PVL occurred in 31.1 and 19.9% (p = 0.046), and new PPI occurred in 13.4 and 15.3%, respectively. Mean gradients remained low among Evolut and Navitor cohorts at 1 year (7.7 and 7.3 mmHg; p = 0.65), whereas effective orifice area was higher among Evolut cohorts at 1 year (2.1 and 1.8 cm2; p < 0.001) (p = p-interaction).

CONCLUSIONS: Navitor and Evolut PRO/PRO+/FX both demonstrated high device success, low mortality, favorable hemodynamic performance, and low rates of moderate or greater PVL at 1-year follow-up. Mild PVL and new PPI remained frequent. Observed comparative signals should be interpreted as indirect hypothesis-generating findings.

title: Right Ventricular Cardiomyocyte Dysfunction and Arrhythmogenesis in a Bleomycin-induced Mouse Model of Group 3 Pulmonary Hypertension.
summary: Group 3 pulmonary hypertension (PH) occurs when lung diseases induce hypoxic vasoconstriction and pulmonary vascular remodeling. The increase in pulmonary vascular resistance elevates right ventricular (RV) afterload leading to progressive ventricular dysfunction. The mechanisms underlying cardiomyocyte dysfunction in Group 3 PH remain poorly characterized, despite RV pathology representing a critical component of disease progression. Using a mouse model of intratracheal bleomycin-induced PH, we tested the hypothesis that RV function and cardiomyocyte excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) are impaired in PH. Male and female mice were administered intratracheal saline (Sham) or bleomycin to induce PH and assess for sex differences across cardiac parameters. Langendorff-perfused working heart preparations revealed that PH mice display greater RV pressure development, elevated end diastolic pressure, and more spontaneous ventricular arrhythmias versus Sham. Structurally, hearts of PH mice exhibited increased RV hypertrophy and fibrosis versus Sham, with the hypertrophic response more pronounced in males versus females. To assess Ca2+ dynamics and cellular contractile function, enzymatically isolated cardiomyocytes were subjected to electrical field stimulation (0.5-4 Hz, fura-2 dye). RV cardiomyocyte ECC was impaired in PH versus Sham mice, including elevated diastolic Ca2+ and shorter diastolic sarcomere lengths, depressed Ca2+ transient and sarcomere contraction amplitudes, and slower Ca2+ decay rates with slower sarcomere relaxation. Left ventricular (LV) cardiomyocytes did not display these changes. Taken together, these data indicate impairment in RV ECC in the bleomycin-induced PH model, highlighting multiple Ca2+ handling abnormalities that may contribute to the RV dysfunction and arrhythmogenesis observed clinically in PH.

title: Genetic variants of transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy associated with low sensitivity to bone scintigraphy: a systematic review.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA) is characterized by amyloid deposition and frequently leads to a progressive cardiomyopathy with poor prognosis. Bone scintigraphy with 99mTc-labeled tracers is the cornerstone of noninvasive diagnosis, yet several hereditary TTR variants are associated with false-negative or low-grade tracer uptake.

OBJECTIVES: To identify all TTR variants associated with false-negative bone scintigraphy in hereditary ATTR-CA and discuss clinical implications.

METHODS: Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane were searched from inception to July 2025 per PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included observational studies, case series, and case reports of patients with confirmed ATTR-CA undergoing TTR genetic testing and 99mTc scintigraphy.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies (108 patients) met inclusion criteria. Thirteen pathogenic TTR variants were associated with low or absent uptake (Perugini grade 0-1); p.Val50Met, p.Phe84Leu, and p.Ser97Tyr were most consistently implicated, while p.Val142Ile showed false-negative results in ∼5-10% of carriers. In 11 of 13 variants, advanced structural cardiomyopathy was confirmed despite negative scintigraphy.

CONCLUSIONS: Bone scintigraphy has important limitations in specific hereditary TTR variants. A negative scan does not exclude cardiac involvement in genetically at-risk patients. Multimodal strategies including CMR and histological assessment are essential for timely diagnosis.

title: NLRP3 inflammasome-driven inflammation as a cause of atrial fibrillation: potential synergistic inhibition of the NLRP3 via upstream magnesium repletion and targeting NLRP3 with a downstream inhibitor.
summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent sustained cardiac arrhythmia. Current therapeutic approaches (antiarrhythmic/rate control medications, anticoagulation, cardioversion, catheter ablation, and cardiac surgery) are effective in selected patients but are associated with adverse effects and significant recurrence rates. These limitations underscore the need for novel adjunctive therapeutic strategies. Substantial biomarker and histopathologic evidence demonstrates chronic inflammation in AF; however, the mechanisms that initiate and sustain this process remain incompletely defined. Emerging evidence suggests that cytokine-driven innate immune activation, rather than adaptive autoimmune mechanisms, is involved, supporting the concept that AF represents a previously unrecognized autoinflammatory disorder. The most widely studied inflammasome protein in AF is NLRP3, a central regulator of innate immunity and a key mechanism controlling the release of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 that can initiate influx of inflammatory cells causing unchecked inflammation and end-stage fibrosis. Intracellular calcium (Ca2+) can stimulate the NLRP3 inflammasome, which can be inhibited upstream by elemental magnesium (Mg2+). The hypothesis proposes that AF is, in part, a dysregulated autoinflammatory condition driven by persistent activation of NLRP3 inflammasome (NLRP3) from endogenous danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) derived from common cardiometabolic conditions, such as obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, along with AF triggers, especially excessive alcohol and tobacco consumption. Furthermore, NLRP3-mediated inflammation, combined with Mg2+ deficiency, may contribute to an energy deficit in sinoatrial (SA) node cardiomyocytes, thereby impairing the electrical automaticity that generates sinus rhythm (SR). Lastly, it is hypothesized reduced AF burden may occur by a synergistic therapeutic strategy combining pharmacokinetic-based oral Mg2+ supplementation with downstream inhibitors of NLRP3. Reports in the medical literature indicating inconsistent clinical efficacy of oral Mg2+ controlling AF may reflect underappreciation of Mg2+ pharmacokinetics involving slow intracellular repletion, and suboptimal Mg2+ formulations. Addressing these factors may bridge the translational gap and enable standardized oral Mg2+ based adjunctive therapy for AF.

title: Placental transcriptomes differ in human pregnancies complicated by severe fetal left heart obstruction.
summary: The etiology of severe left-sided obstructive lesions (LSOL) of the heart, a common form of congenital heart disease (CHD), often remains unknown even after comprehensive genetic testing. Preclinical models implicate placental perturbations in abnormal cardiogenesis; however, little is known about connections between human placenta and fetal cardiac diseases. We profiled term placentas from severe LSOL pregnancies (n = 20) with and without placental pathologies and healthy controls (n = 10) to test whether severe fetal LSOL is associated with distinct transcriptomic and cellular states. Bulk RNA-sequencing of archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues identified 1,030 differentially expressed protein-coding genes (580 [up], 450 [down]). Upregulated programs involved heart-valve development, endothelial signaling, and extracellular-matrix processes; while endocrine, trophoblast and gamma-aminobutyric acid signaling processes were downregulated. Severe LSOL pregnancies with histologically normal placentas showed enrichment of lymphatic-vascular development and cyclic-nucleotide signaling. Digital deconvolution analysis inferred reduced trophoblast fractions with reciprocal increase in endothelial and immune cell types. These findings support a unique placental gene expression in abnormal cardiac development, even in the absence of overt placental histopathology. These RNA expression signatures may serve as candidate biomarkers and lay the groundwork for mechanistic studies of the heart-placenta axis and future risk stratification in pregnancies with fetuses diagnosed with severe LSOL.

title: De Rol van het Epigenoom in de Ontwikkeling van Atriumfibrilleren bij de Mens Ontrafelen met behulp van Single-Nucleus Omics
summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia. Its development and persistence depend partly on atrial myopathy, which encompasses structural, contractile, and electrophysiological abnormalities. However, the cellular and regulatory changes associated with AF are difficult to distinguish from those accompanying structural atrial remodelling. This thesis investigated these overlapping processes in human left and right atrial appendages using single-nucleus transcriptomics, paired RNA and chromatin-accessibility profiling, histology and functional experiments. The first study benchmarked computational methods for recovering donor identity after pooling samples for single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Vireo provided the best overall balance of accuracy, robustness, and usability among the methods evaluated. This framework enabled the second study, which established an atlas comprising 25,119 nuclei from 24 left atrial appendage samples and 50,535 nuclei from 36 right atrial appendage samples. Paired transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility measurements covered 12,189 nuclei from 20 left atrial appendage samples. Participants were stratified by rhythm and left atrial volume index (LAVI), allowing comparisons between rhythm-associated and enlargement-associated changes. Major cell populations were shared between appendages, but disease-associated transcriptional programmes differed between chambers. Histology supported an association between high LAVI and greater left atrial fibrosis. Multiomic analysis identified a stressed cardiomyocyte state expressing NPPA and NPPB, enriched in participants with both AF and high LAVI, and nominated CTCF as a candidate regulator of the associated chromatin landscape. Six fibroblast states included an inflammatory PTGDS-positive population. Regulatory-network analyses prioritised TWIST2, TBX20 and GLIS3 as candidate regulators of fibroblast-state transitions. JMJD1C emerged as an epigenetic candidate enriched in PTGDS-positive fibroblasts and responsive to TGF-β1. Its depletion in primary human cardiac fibroblasts altered the global H3K9me2 response, reduced α-SMA positivity, and reshaped selected TGF-β1-responsive transcriptional programmes. Computational analysis additionally predicted macrophage-to-fibroblast TGF-β signalling. Together, these findings show that AF and structural atrial remodelling have overlapping but distinct cellular and regulatory correlates. They identify JMJD1C as a functional regulator of fibroblast activation and a candidate for further therapeutic investigation, rather than an established treatment target.

title: Shared genetic architecture between digestive infectious diseases and cardiovascular diseases: a genome-wide cross-trait analysis
summary: Background Digestive infectious diseases and cardiovascular diseases may share common genetic, inflammatory and immune-related mechanisms. However, the shared genetic architecture between these disease groups, the specific pleiotropic loci involved and the potential contribution of intestinal infectious diseases (IID) to cardiovascular risk remain incompletely understood. Methods We analysed publicly available genome-wide association study summary statistics for 36 binary traits of European ancestry, including 16 digestive infectious disease traits and 20 cardiovascular traits. Univariate linkage disequilibrium score regression was used to estimate SNP-based heritability and prioritise traits. Global and local genetic sharing were evaluated using cross-trait LDSC and SUPERGNOVA. Multi-trait analysis of GWAS, cross-trait sensitivity analyses, FM-summary fine-mapping and Bayesian colocalisation were used to identify and refine pleiotropic loci. Candidate genes and biological functions were investigated using MAGMA, tissue- and cell-type-specific enrichment analyses, transcriptome-wide association analysis and protein-wide association analysis. Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomisation and two-step mediation analyses using three independent gut microbiome GWAS resources were subsequently performed. Results Sixteen traits passed heritability quality control, yielding 39 trait pairs with significant global genetic correlations after Bonferroni correction. MTAG identified 41 candidate SNP records and 14 trait-pair-specific lead-SNP records representing eight unique SNPs; 39 candidate records and 12 lead records involved IID. Fine-mapping and colocalisation prioritised eight records representing four unique variants. Locus-based gene prioritisation retained 24 candidate genes across four pairs. Gene-set enrichment identified 43 significant trait-pair-GO term associations, and tissue enrichment identified seven significant associations. Transcriptome-wide analyses implicated 21 candidate genes, and proteome-wide analyses identified four associations involving three proteins. After false discovery rate (FDR) correction, forward MR supported associations of IID liability with cardiac arrhythmias, myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation and flutter, and ischaemic heart disease; reverse MR supported only cardiac arrhythmias to IID. Five positive exploratory microbiota-IID-cardiovascular mediation patterns were described. Only the Oxalobacter-IID-cardiac arrhythmias indirect effect reached unadjusted P < 0.05. Conclusions Digestive infectious diseases, particularly IID, share substantial genetic architecture with cardiovascular diseases. Integrative genetic analyses identified recurrent pleiotropic loci, candidate genes and putative microbiome-mediated pathways linking IID with cardiovascular outcomes. These findings provide testable hypotheses for further functional validation and clinical investigation.

title: Spliceosome gene mutations synergize with anthracyclines to amplify atrial fibrillation risk in hematologic malignancies: a multicenter cohort study with discovery and validation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a life‑threatening complication in patients with hematologic malignancies, yet personalized risk stratification remains challenging. Spliceosome gene mutations are key drivers of these malignancies, but their specific role in AF pathogenesis and potential synergy with anthracyclines is unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included a discovery cohort (n = 1160) and a validation cohort (n = 412). Multivariable Cox regression, Fine‑Gray competing risk models, and false discovery rate (FDR) correction were used to assess the association between clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP)-related mutations (DTA, spliceosome, and DNA damage repair genes) and AF. To avoid immortal time bias, anthracycline exposure was treated as a time-dependent covariate. Interaction analysis was used to evaluate the synergistic effect between spliceosome mutations and anthracyclines. Mechanistic exploration was performed using monocyte‑atrial fibroblast co‑culture and western blotting.

RESULTS: In the discovery cohort, spliceosome mutations were significantly associated with AF (sHR = 1.67, 95% CI: 1.09-2.55, FDR q = 0.029). This association remained robust after sensitivity analyses, and was confirmed in the validation cohort (sHR = 6.26, 95% CI: 1.52-25.8, FDR q = 0.022). A significant synergistic interaction was observed between spliceosome mutations and anthracycline exposure: in the discovery cohort, the time‑dependent competing risk model (adjusted for age, sex, disease subtype) yielded an sHR of 3.68 (95% CI: 1.23-10.9, P = 0.019), with consistent results in the validation cohort (sHR = 5.14, 95% CI: 1.29-20.6, P = 0.021). The interaction remained robust in sensitivity analyses. Exploratory analyses showed that patients with spliceosome mutations had larger left atrial diameter and higher monocyte counts (both FDR q < 0.05), with monocyte counts positively correlated with IL‑6 levels. In vitro, monocytes from mutation carriers promoted COL1A1 and α‑SMA expression in atrial fibroblasts, an effect attenuated by IL‑6 neutralization.

CONCLUSIONS: Spliceosome gene mutations appear to be a novel independent predictor of AF in patients with hematologic malignancies and show a synergistic effect with anthracyclines in increasing AF risk. Myeloid-driven inflammation and atrial remodeling likely contribute to this process. These findings suggest that enhanced AF surveillance could be considered in spliceosome-mutated patients receiving anthracyclines, and that inflammation may represent a potential therapeutic target for cardioprotection.
